en: The President signs a bill passed by Congress to turn it into an official law.
Hanging the Philippine flag with the red stripe on top signals that the country is at war.
General Emilio Aguinaldo waved the Philippine flag from his balcony to officially declare independence from Spain.
The Ifugao people carved mountain steps and built irrigation canals to channel mountain springs into their rice terraces.
Dr. Fe del Mundo used a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in hospitals lacking electricity.
Farmers in Lucban decorate their houses with colorful kiping leaves to thank San Isidro Labrador for a good harvest.
Citizens who reach eighteen years old and register can vote to choose their local and national government leaders.
Ancient Filipinos carved Baybayin symbols on bamboo to write letters, where each symbol represents a syllable rather than a single letter.
Neighbors physically carry a traditional nipa hut on their shoulders to help a family relocate to a new area.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The Supreme Court reviews new laws to ensure they do not violate the rules written in the Philippine Constitution.
Farmers use the strong carabao to pull heavy wooden plows through muddy fields to prepare the soil for planting rice.
